title: Dyosa Ampalaya (Diyosa ampalaya): Characteristics
metaDescription: Dyosa ampalaya is an open pollinated ampalaya variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Dyosa ampalaya is an open pollinated ampalaya variety, also sold or known as Diyosa ampalaya. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Harbest Agribusiness (Seeds of Hope).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Dyosa ampalaya is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Diyosa ampalaya, this is the same ampalaya. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [ampalaya variety finder](/crop-varieties/ampalaya), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 55 to 60 days after sowing. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit ampalaya fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of the best sellers in Harbest's Seeds of Hope catalogue. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual ampalaya on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Dyosa ampalaya

Pick by fruit: long and light green for most markets, short and dark for the bitter lovers. Hybrids yield more on a trellis, and some are bred to tolerate the downy mildew of the wet season. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Diyosa ampalaya the same as Dyosa?
items.a: Yes. Diyosa ampalaya is another name for Dyosa. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Dyosa?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
